summary.text: OPT (Open Pre-trained Transformers) is a suite of decoder-only language models from Meta, ranging from 125 million to 175 billion parameters, released on 3 May 2022 together with the metaseq code used to train them. The sizes up to 66B were released for download under a non-commercial licence; OPT-175B went to approved researchers on request.

summary.text: LLaMA is a set of large language models for text from Meta, released on 24 February 2023 in sizes of 7B, 13B, 33B and 65B parameters to help researchers study such models. The weights were shared case by case with approved researchers under a non-commercial licence; from the Llama 2 launch on, Meta calls it Llama 1.

summary.text: Llama 2 is the second generation of Meta's Llama language models for text, released on 18 July 2023 at 7B, 13B and 70B parameters, each with a dialogue-tuned Llama 2-Chat version. Meta made the weights free for research and commercial use and, with Microsoft as preferred partner, offered the models through Azure, AWS, Hugging Face and other providers.

summary.text: Meta Llama 3 is the third generation of Meta's Llama language models, released on 18 April 2024 as open weights in 8B and 70B sizes, each pretrained and instruction-tuned, under the custom Llama 3 Community License. Meta also offered it through cloud partners and said its Meta AI assistant was built with Llama 3 technology.

summary.text: Llama 3.1 is a collection of Meta language models in 8B, 70B and 405B sizes, released on 23 July 2024 as open weights under the custom Llama 3.1 Community License and through more than 25 partners. It upgraded the Meta Llama 3 8B and 70B models, added a 405B model and raised the context length to 128K tokens, with support for eight languages.

Quantized builds of the 1B and 3B Instruct models followed on 24 October 2024, limited to 8K context for mobile devices.

summary.text: Llama 3.2 is a set of open-weight Meta models released on 25 September 2024: text-only 1B and 3B models aimed at on-device use, and 11B and 90B Vision models, which Meta describes as the first Llama models to support vision tasks. The small models were distilled from Llama 3.1, and the Vision models add an image adapter to Llama 3.1 text models.

summary.text: Llama 4 Behemoth is a mixture-of-experts model in Meta's Llama 4 line, previewed in April 2025 while still in training, which Meta said it was not yet releasing. Meta describes it as multimodal, with 16 experts and 288B of nearly two trillion parameters active, and used it as the teacher model for distilling Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick.

summary.text: Muse Spark is the first model in Meta's Muse series, built by Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta describes it as a natively multimodal reasoning model with tool use; it launched in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai with Instant and Thinking modes, and select partners got a private API preview.

access.note: API access through the public preview of the Meta Model API launched with this model; in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai it was available in Thinking mode.

summary.text: Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model in Meta's Muse series that Meta says is built for agentic tasks. It succeeded the first Muse Spark in Meta AI and launched with the public preview of the Meta Model API, which lists it as muse-spark-1.1 with text, image, video, audio and PDF input and a 1,048,576-token context window.

access.note: Available in the Meta Model API (with expanded global access) and in the Muse Code terminal agent, which runs on that API.

features.note: Reasoning model with adjustable reasoning_effort from minimal to xhigh; reasoning cannot be disabled.

changes.text: Meta says it scaled up training compute on coding tasks, with more varied training environments and long-horizon tasks such as whole-repository generation.
Co-trained with the Muse Code agent harness so that it works with that agent's tools, goals, compaction and subagents.
Meta says it follows complex instructions more precisely, helped by training data that Muse Spark 1.1 generated and graded.
Also offered on a discounted Contributor tier that lets Meta train on customer prompts and completions; Muse Spark 1.1 has no such tier.

summary.text: Muse Spark 1.2 is a multimodal reasoning model in Meta's Muse series that Meta describes as a coding-focused update to Muse Spark 1.1. It was released with Muse Code, a terminal coding agent in beta that it powers, and the Meta Model API offers it on a Standard tier and a discounted Contributor tier that lets Meta train on prompts and completions.

It accepts text and images and reasons before answering; Meta says it was distilled from Muse Spark outputs and aims it at local agent workflows on a Mac or PC with a single consumer GPU.

summary.text: Muse Spark 1.3 is a multimodal reasoning model in Meta's Muse series, offered in the Meta Model API and the Muse Code terminal agent. description.text: Meta Platforms, Inc., named Facebook, Inc. until October 2021, runs apps including Facebook, Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp. Its FAIR research team dates from late 2013.
